fig1_lever_rule.svg: Inside the dome the mixture is just a mass-weighted blend of saturated liquid and saturated vapour, so $y=y_f+x\,y_{fg}$ for EVERY specific property (mixture_property). Scaling each by its own $f\!-\!g$ span, the specific volume, enthalpy and entropy of water at 10 bar all land on the same diagonal. This is the lever rule, and it is what makes the tables usable: measure any one property, invert the line (quality_from_property), and every other property follows. The latent heat here is 2015 kJ/kg.
fig2_liquid_volume_fraction.svg: Quality is a MASS fraction, and at 10 bar a kilogram of steam occupies 172 times the volume of a kilogram of water. The consequence (liquid_volume_fraction) is that the two book-keepings diverge violently: a vessel that is half evaporated by mass is still 0.6% liquid by volume, and the sight-glass barely moves until the quality is close to 1. Reading a level gauge as if it showed quality is a classic error; the module's quality() takes masses precisely to keep the distinction explicit.
